prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the Drop component is a regular <div> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for div elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/div) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)

How to align the drop with respect to the target element. Not specifying a vertical or horizontal alignment will cause it to be aligned in the center.

To prevent creating a new object on each render, the align property should be persistent, either as a static constant outside of the render function or memo-ized using hooks.

For more guidance on when and how to memoize,read the React documentation on the useMemo hook. For using a static constant, see ourDrop component Storybook examples.
